title: The Man Who Became a Star
subtitle: A violent story explains a low star in the west

learningObjectives.text: Why does the hunter call for the ravine to close?
How does the story end for the old man?

star.author: Greenlandic storytellers, collected by Knud Rasmussen
star.locator: The Man Who Became A Star; The Man Who Became A Star, normalized characters 26-1253
star.excerpt: There was once an old man who stood out on the ice waiting for the seal to come up to their breathing holes to breathe. But on the shore, just opposite where he was, a crowd of children were playing in a ravine, and time after time they frightened away a seal just as he was about to harpoon it. At last the old man grew angry with them for thus spoiling his catch, and cried out: "Close up, Ravine, over those who are spoiling my hunting." And at once the hillside closed over those children at play. One of them, who was carrying a little brother, had her fur coat torn. Then they all fell to screaming inside the hill, for they could not come out. And none could bring them food, only water that they were able to pour down a crack, and this they licked up from the sides. At last they all died of hunger. And now the neighbours fell upon that old man who had shut up the children by magic in the hill. He took to flight, and the others ran after him. But all at once he became bright, and rose up to heaven as a great star. We can see it now, in the west, when the lights begin to return after the great darkness. But it is low down, and never climbs high in the sky. And we call it Nâlaussartoq: he who stands and listens.
star.note: Verbatim English rendering by Worster from stories collected by Rasmussen in Greenland. The book title uses an outdated ethnonym; this lesson identifies the collection's Greenland scope.

narrativeBlocks.title: Children disturb a hunt
narrativeBlocks.body: An old hunter becomes angry when children repeatedly frighten seals away from his harpoon. He calls for the ravine to close over them.

narrativeBlocks.title: A transformation after pursuit
narrativeBlocks.body: The story says the old man flees from the neighbours, becomes a bright star, and remains low in the western sky as the lights return after darkness.

narrativeBlocks.title: Treat the violence plainly
narrativeBlocks.body: This collection records a particular Greenland story with a violent outcome. Do not generalize it into a belief shared by all Inuit communities or soften the event into an abstract 'moral.'

narrativeBlocks.title: The story names a visible star
narrativeBlocks.body: The narrator gives the name Nélaussartoq and glosses it as 'he who stands and listens'; keep that attribution within Rasmussen's collection.
